title: A visual system emerges
description: In western Europe, recognizable coats of arms become associated with individual identity, seals, and knightly display.

title: Armorial rolls proliferate
description: Written and illustrated records begin assembling shields and bearers into increasingly systematic collections.

title: Heraldry moves far beyond war
description: Armorial seals and symbols flourish in ecclesiastical, civic, and other institutional settings.

title: The College of Arms is incorporated
description: England's College of Arms receives its charter and continues as an official heraldic institution.

title: Visitations and recording
description: English heraldic visitations seek to examine pedigrees and the use of arms, illustrating the administrative side of armory.

title: Scotland's armorial register begins
description: The Public Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland begins under the Court of the Lord Lyon.

title: The scholarship of arms expands
description: Printed armorials, manuals, and antiquarian societies help catalogue and interpret heraldic evidence.

title: The Heraldry Society is founded
description: A modern educational charity develops publications, lectures, and tools for serious public study.

title: A Canadian authority
description: The Canadian Heraldic Authority is established, expanding Canada's own grants and public register.

title: Heraldry becomes computational
description: Digital registers, vector illustration, and searchable archives make historic and contemporary armory more accessible.
